akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿طِبَاقاً﴾, and its singular is "الطَبَق".

akhfash:4-4.t: He said ﴿خَاسِئاً وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ﴾ because you say "خَسَأْتُهُ" ("I drove him off"), so "خَسَأ" ("he was driven off"), so ﴿هُوَ خَاسِيء﴾ ("he is driven off").

akhfash:18-18.t: And He said ﴿فَكَيْفَ كَانَ نكِيرِ﴾, that is: My disapproval (إِنكارِي).

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿إِلَى ٱلطَّيْرِ فَوْقَهُمْ صَافَّاتٍ﴾: He used the plural because "الطَيْر" (birds) is a group, like your saying "صاحِب" and "صَحْب", "شَاهِد" and "شَهْد", "رَاكِب" and "رَكْب".

akhfash:27-27.t: And He said ﴿هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِ تَدَّعُونَ﴾ because they used to say ﴿رَبَّنَا عَجِّل لَّنَا قِطَّنَا﴾ and ﴿ٱئْتِنَا بِعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, so it was said to them when they saw the punishment: ﴿هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِ تَدْعُونَ﴾ — light (without doubling) — and ﴿تَدَّعُونَ﴾ — heavy (with doubling). People read it in this meaning; it is better, and it is how we read, because it is one thing after another. «[Translator's note: i.e., the doubled form expresses calling for one thing after another, repeatedly.]»

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿مَآؤُكُمْ غَوْراً فَمَن يَأْتِيكُمْ بِمَآءٍ مَّعِينٍ﴾, that is: sinking away (غائرا); but He described it with the maṣdar (verbal noun). And you say "لَيْلَةٌ غَمٌّ" ("a night of gloom"), meaning "غَامَّةٌ" ("gloomy").

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿بِيَدِهِ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿الْمُلْكُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قدير»; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ khabar, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ badal (substitute); ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿الْمَوْتَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَالْحَياةَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الموت». ﴿لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit «أن» after the lām of purpose (lām al-taʿlīl), the fāʿil being latent and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلق»; ﴿أَيُّكُمْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَحْسَنُ﴾ its khabar (predicate); ﴿عَمَلًا﴾ tamyīz (specification), and the nominal clause is the second object of «يبلوكم»; ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفُورُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its two khabars, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a second badal (substitute) for the relative noun; ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to «سموات», and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿طِباقاً﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «سبع»; ﴿ما تَرى﴾ «ما» is negating, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿فِي خَلْقِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿مِنْ تَفاوُتٍ﴾ genitive (majrūr) in form by the redundant (zāʾida) «من», accusative (manṣūb) in position as the object of «ترى», and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿فَارْجِعِ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿الْبَصَرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿هَلْ تَرى﴾ «هل» is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿مِنْ فُطُورٍ﴾ «فطور» is genitive in form by the redundant «من», accusative in position as the object of «ترى», and the clause is in the position of an accusative by an omitted verb.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ﴾ «ثم» is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿كَرَّتَيْنِ﴾ a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object); ﴿يَنْقَلِبْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْبَصَرَ﴾ fāʿil «[Translator's note: the quoted word is printed with a fatḥa in the source; in the verse it is «الْبَصَرُ», nominative.]»; ﴿خاسِئاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا السَّماءَ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of oath, and the lām falls in the answer to the omitted oath; ﴿قد﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ a naʿt (adjective); ﴿بِمَصابِيحَ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «زيّنا», and the clause is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَجَعَلْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; ﴿رُجُوماً﴾ its second object; ﴿لِلشَّياطِينِ﴾ both are attached to «رجوما», and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to the clause «زيّنا», with no grammatical position; ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿عَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, annexed to ﴿السَّعِيرِ﴾, muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct).

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَلِلَّذِينَ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِرَبِّهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين»; ﴿عَذابُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿إِذا أُلْقُوا﴾ «إذا» is an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive, and a passive past verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿فِيها﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿سَمِعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿لَها﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿شَهِيقاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَهِيَ تَفُورُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿تَكادُ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿تَمَيَّزُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «تكاد», and the clause «تكاد..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مِنَ الْغَيْظِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿كُلَّما﴾: a conditional particle that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿أُلْقِيَ﴾ a passive past verb; ﴿فِيها﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿فَوْجٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿سَأَلَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿خَزَنَتُها﴾ its fāʿil, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ﴾ the hamza is for the interrogative of rebuke (al-istifhām al-tawbīkhī), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the kāf being the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿نَذِيرٌ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is the second object of «سأل».

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer; ﴿قَدْ جاءَنا نَذِيرٌ﴾ «قد» is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), and a past verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿فَكَذَّبْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَقُلْنا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «كذبنا»; ﴿ما نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ﴾ «ما» is negating, and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ «شيء» is genitive (majrūr) in form by the redundant (zāʾida) «من», accusative (manṣūb) in position as mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the object of the saying; ﴿إِنْ﴾ negating; ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿كَبِيرٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, not making the verb jussive; ﴿كُنَّا نَسْمَعُ﴾ «كان» and its noun, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «كنا», and the clause «كنا..» is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿أَوْ﴾ conjunctive; ﴿نَعْقِلُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «نسمع»; ﴿ما﴾ negating; ﴿كُنَّا﴾ «كان» and its noun; ﴿فِي أَصْحابِ﴾ the khabar of «كنا»; ﴿السَّعِيرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause «ما كنا..» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. And the clause «لو» with what follows it is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فَاعْتَرَفُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِذَنْبِهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَسُحْقاً﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿سحقا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; ﴿لِأَصْحابِ﴾ both are attached to «سحقا»; ﴿السَّعِيرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct).

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿يَخْشَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿رَبَّهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿مَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause is the khabar of «إنّ», and the clause «إنّ» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَأَجْرٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «مغفرة»; ﴿كَبِيرٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَأَسِرُّوا قَوْلَكُمْ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَوِ﴾ conjunctive; ﴿اجْهَرُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أسروا»; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ «إنّ», its noun and its khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿بِذاتِ﴾ both are attached to «عليم»; ﴿الصُّدُورِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct).

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿أَلا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ﴾ «ألا» is a particle of opening (istiftāḥ), and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its two khabars (predicates), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿جَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿ذَلُولًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فَامْشُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿فِي مَناكِبِها﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَكُلُوا مِنْ رِزْقِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ﴾ a fronted khabar and a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿أَأَمِنْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is interrogative, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فِي السَّماءِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿أَنْ يَخْسِفَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن»; ﴿بِكُمُ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of an accusative as a badal (substitute) for the relative noun. ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿إذا﴾ of surprise (fujāʾiyya); ﴿هِيَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿تَمُورُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿أَمْ أَمِنْتُمْ﴾ «أم» is a conjunction meaning «بل», and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿مَنْ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فِي السَّماءِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿أَنْ يُرْسِلَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن»; ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿حاصِباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of an accusative as a badal (substitute) for the relative noun; ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun, fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿نَذِيرِ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, which has been dropped for lightness, and the nominal clause stands in place of the object of «تعلمون».

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition, the lām falls in the answer to the oath, and «قد» is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); ﴿كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition); ﴿كيف﴾ an interrogative noun, the fronted khabar (predicate) of «كان»; ﴿كانَ﴾ «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿نَكِيرِ﴾ its noun, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ, which has been dropped for lightness, and the clause is the apodosis of the implied condition, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle and the wāw is resumptive; ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the statement is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿إِلَى الطَّيْرِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿صافَّاتٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿يَقْبِضْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, the nūn of the feminine plural being its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ما يُمْسِكُهُنَّ﴾ «ما» is negating, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ both are attached to «بصير»; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿أَمَّنْ﴾ «أم» is a conjunction meaning «بل», and «من» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿هذَا﴾ the demonstrative is khabar (predicate); ﴿الَّذِي﴾ the relative noun is a badal (substitute) for «هذا»; ﴿هُوَ جُنْدٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «جند»; ﴿يَنْصُرُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the clause is a second naʿt of «جند»; ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿إِنِ﴾ negating; ﴿الْكافِرُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿فِي غُرُورٍ﴾ khabar, and the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿أَمَّنْ هذَا الَّذِي﴾ its i'rab has been given before; ﴿يَرْزُقُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿إِنْ أَمْسَكَ﴾ «إن» is a conditional particle making the verb jussive, and a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted; ﴿رِزْقَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿بَلْ لَجُّوا﴾ «بل» is a particle of conjunction and transition (intiqāl), and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿فِي عُتُوٍّ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿وَنُفُورٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «عتو», and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿أَفَمَنْ﴾ the hamza is interrogative, the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, «من» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَمْشِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مُكِبًّا﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿عَلى وَجْهِهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مكبا»; ﴿أَهْدى﴾ khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَمَّنْ﴾ «أم» is a conjunction and «من» is mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَمْشِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿سَوِيًّا﴾ ḥāl; ﴿عَلى صِراطٍ﴾ both are attached to «سويا»; ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is omitted because what precedes indicates it, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿أَنْشَأَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿وَجَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿السَّمْعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ﴾ both are conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «السمع», and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿ما﴾ redundant (zāʾida); ﴿تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause, giving the reason (taʿlīliyya), has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿ذَرَأَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil being latent; ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ﴾ both are attached to «تحشرون»; ﴿تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مَتى﴾ an interrogative noun, fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿هذَا﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الْوَعْدُ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ conditional, making the verb jussive, and «كان» and its noun; ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, and the conditional sentence is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ the restraining and the restrained (kāffa makfūfa); ﴿الْعِلْمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿وَإِنَّما﴾ and the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِنَّما أَنَا نَذِيرٌ﴾ «إنما» is the restraining and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «نذير», and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لما﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿رَأَوْهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿زُلْفَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿سِيئَتْ﴾ a passive past verb; ﴿وُجُوهُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb; ﴿هذَا الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ «كان» and its noun; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تدعون»; ﴿تَدَّعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of «كنتم», and the clause «كنتم..» is the ṣila of the relative noun, and the clause «قيل..» is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī), and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional, making the verb jussive; ﴿أَهْلَكَنِيَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the Name of Majesty being its fāʿil, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the yāʾ of the first person; ﴿مَعِيَ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿رَحِمَنا﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يُجِيرُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿الْكافِرِينَ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مِنْ عَذابٍ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب», and the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, and the conditional clause stands in place of the two objects of «أرأيتم».

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿هُوَ الرَّحْمنُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَعَلَيْهِ﴾ both are attached to «توكلنا»; ﴿تَوَكَّلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مَنْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of «تعلمون», and the clause «ستعلمون..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ its i'rab has been given before; ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional, making the verb jussive; ﴿أَصْبَحَ ماؤُكُمْ غَوْراً﴾ «أصبح», its noun and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿من﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَأْتِيكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis; ﴿بِماءٍ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿مَعِينٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «ماء».

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱعْتَرَفُواْ بِذَنبِهِمْ﴾.
He did not say "بذنوبهم", because ذنب contains [the sense of] an action (fiʿl), and every such [noun] that you attach to a people, being an action, stands for all their actions. Do you not see that you say: قد أذنب القوم إذنابا (the people have sinned a sinning), and within the meaning of إذناب are [many] sins? Likewise you say: خرجَتْ أعطيته الناس and عطاء الناس (the people's stipends / the people's stipend came out), and the meaning is one. And Allah knows best.
His saying: ﴿فَسُحْقاً لأَصْحَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ﴾. They agreed on reading السُّحْق light; had it been read فسُحُقاً, it would be a good dialect form.
[Translator's note: «أعطيته الناس» is as printed, presumably for «أعطيات الناس» ("the people's stipends").]

farraa:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱمْشُواْ فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا﴾: in its sides.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿أَأَمِنتُمْ﴾: it is permissible here to put between the two alifs an alif without hamza, as is said: ﴿آانتم﴾, ﴿آإذ مِتْنا﴾. Likewise, do so with every two vowelled hamzas: add a lengthening (madda) between them. This is from the dialect of Banū Tamīm.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلاً﴾.
He did not make the "testing" act upon أىّ, because between أى and the testing a verb is implied, as you say in speech: بلوتكم لأنظر أيُّكم أطوع (I tested you to see which of you is most obedient). So it is the same here: make [the verb] operate on what you see before it, i.e. on what allows "seeing" to be implied, as in your saying: اعلم أيُّهم ذهب (find out which of them went) [202/a] and the like. Likewise His saying: ﴿سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهم بِذَلِكَ زَعِيمٌ﴾: He means: ask them, then see which of them will guarantee that. "Saying" may also serve in the place of "seeing" in your saying اعلم أيهم ذهب, because he comes to them and says: Which of you went? This is the nature of this chapter, and it has been explained elsewhere than here. But if you said: اضرب أيّهم ذهب (strike whichever of them went), it would be accusative, because "striking" cannot bear an implied "seeing", as knowing, asking and testing can.
[Translator's note: «الموض» is as printed, for «الموضع» ("place").]

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَمَن يَمْشِي مُكِبّاً عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِ﴾.
You say: قد أكبَّ الرجل (the man fell on his face) when his action does not fall on anyone else; but when the action is transitive you drop the alif and say: قد كبّه الله لوجهه (Allah threw him on his face), and كببتُه أنا لوجهه (I threw him on his face).

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقِيلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِ تَدَّعُونَ ﴾.
He means: تَدْعُونَ (you call for), and it is like His saying تَذْكُرون and تَذَكَّرون, and تخبرون and تختبرون; the meaning is one, and Allah knows best.
One of the readers read: "ما تَدْخَرون", meaning: تدّخرون. So if a reader read: "هذا الذى كُنتم به تدْعون", it would be correct.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُون﴾.
The reading of the general body [of readers] is "فستعلمون" with tāʾ.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us, he said: I heard al-Farrāʾ, and he mentioned Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl [202/b], from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī (may Allah have mercy on him): فسيعلمون with yāʾ. And both are correct.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلْقِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ مِن تَفَاوُتٍ﴾.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told me, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: one of our companions told me, from Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya al-Juʿfī, from Abū Isḥāq, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read: "من تفوّت".
Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Ḥibbān told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama, that he read: "تفوّت"; and that is the reading of Yaḥyā, the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, the people of Medina and ʿĀṣim.
The people of Basra read: "تفاوتٍ". The two are of one standing, as He said: "ولا تُصَاعِرْ" and "تُصَعّر", and [one says] تعهّدت فلانا and تعاهدته. التفاوت means discrepancy, i.e.: do you see any discrepancy in His creation? Then He said: "so return your sight", although no verb has been mentioned before it to which the "returning" could refer; because He said: "you do not see", it is as if He said: look, then look again. As for الفطور, they are cracks and fissures.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنْ أَصْبَحَ مَآؤُكُمْ غَوْراً﴾.
The Arabs say: ماء غور (sunken water), بئر غور (a sunken well), and ماءان غور (two sunken waters); they do not make it dual or plural: they do not say ماءان غوران, nor مياه أغوار. It is like الزَّوْر: it is said هؤلاء زور فلان (these are so-and-so's visitors) and هؤلاء ضيف فلان (these are so-and-so's guest[s]), meaning: these are his guests and his visitors. That is because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so it is treated like their saying: قوم عدل (just people), قوم رِضا (approved people) and مَقْنَع (satisfactory people).

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿يَنْقَلِبْ إِلَيْكَ البَصَرُ خَاسِئاً﴾.
He means: abased; and it is حسير, worn out — as a camel or camels become exhausted (yaḥsar) when they are made to stand from emaciation and fatigue; they are then الحسرى, whose singular is حسير.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿تَكَادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ الغَيْظِ﴾: it is [almost] torn apart with rage against them.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Mulk (The Dominion)
Makkan
﷽
It has come in the exegesis that it is called ”اَلْمُنْجِيَةَ“ (the Rescuer): it rescues the one who recites it from the punishment of the grave. And it has come in the exegesis that in the Torah (there is): "Sūrat al-Mulk — whoever recites it in a night has done much."

His saying: ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ المُلْكُ﴾ means: He is exalted and magnified.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ المَوْتَ والحَياةَ لِيَبْلُوَكم أيُّكم أحْسَنُ عَمَلا﴾ — what ”أيُّكم“ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) is implied; the meaning is: "that He may test you, and so know which of you is best in deed" — a knowledge of what has (actually) occurred. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, already knew what would come from them, but the recompense becomes due through the actual occurrence of the deed from them. ”أيُّ“ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it does not govern it, because it retains its original interrogative sense. This is like His saying: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحْصى لِما لَبِثُوا أمَدًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 12]. According to the grammarians this is to be construed as naming (al-tasmiya) [Translator's note: so printed; the expected term is al-taswiya, "equivalence", i.e. the interrogative of alternatives]: its meaning is the meaning of the (interrogative) alif with ”أمْ“. When you say "قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أيُّكم أفْضَلُ" (I know which of you is better), the meaning is "I know whether Zayd is better or ʿAmr"; ”عَلِمْتُ“ does not govern what comes after the alif, and likewise it does not govern ”أيُّ“; the meaning is the same. The meaning of ﴿خَلَقَ المَوْتَ والحَياةَ﴾ is: He created life for you to test you in it, and created death to raise you and requite you for your deeds. It has come in the exegesis of al-Kalbī: He created death in the form of a black-and-white ram; it passes by nothing but that it dies, treads on nothing but that it dies, and nothing finds its scent but that it dies. And He created life in the form of a piebald mare, larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule; it passes by nothing but that it brings it to life, treads on nothing but that it brings it to life, and nothing finds its scent but that it comes to life. And Allah knows best the reality of that.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقًا ما تَرى في خَلْقِ الرَّحْمَنِ مِن تَفاوُتٍ﴾ — it is also read ”فِي خَلْقِ الرَّحْمَنِ مِن تَفَوُّتٍ“, without alif. In ﴿تَفاوُتٍ﴾ ”تَفاؤُتٍ“ is also permissible, with hamza, the hamza substituting for the wāw with ḍamma. One says ”تَفاوَتَ الشَّيْءُ تَفاوُتًا“ and ”تَفَوَّتَ تَفَوُّتًا“ when a thing is inconsistent. So the meaning is: "You see in His creation of the heaven no inconsistency and no disorder." The meaning of ”طِباقًا“ is: layered one upon another; ”طِباقٌ“ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ”طُوبِقَتْ طِباقًا“.

His saying: ﴿فارْجِعِ البَصَرَ هَلْ تَرى مِن فُطُورٍ﴾ means: do you see in it any gaps or cracks?

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ البَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ يَنْقَلِبْ إلَيْكَ البَصَرُ خاسِئًا وهو حَسِيرٌ﴾ — ”خاسِئًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its meaning is "humbled." ”وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ“: it has grown weary before it could see any flaw in the heaven.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا﴾ means: the one, of the seven heavens, that is near (tadnū) to you.

His saying: ﴿بِمَصابِيحَ﴾ means the stars.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ وبِئْسَ المَصِيرُ﴾ — ”عَذابُ جَهَنَّمَ“ is (read) with the accusative and the nominative. The accusative is by conjunction with His saying: "وَأعْتَدْنا لَهم عَذابَ السَّعِيرِ ولِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ عَذابَ جَهَنَّمَ", i.e. "and We have prepared for those who disbelieve in their Lord the punishment of Hell."

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إذا أُلْقُوا فِيها سَمِعُوا لَها شَهِيقًا﴾ — and that (shahīq) is the ugliest of sounds; it is like the braying of a donkey.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿تَكادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ الغَيْظِ﴾ means: it almost bursts apart from its rage against them.

His saying: ﴿كُلَّما أُلْقِيَ فِيها فَوْجٌ سَألَهم خَزَنَتُها ألَمْ يَأْتِكم نَذِيرٌ﴾ ﴿قالُوا بَلى قَدْ جاءَنا نَذِيرٌ﴾ [al-Mulk: 9] — this rebuke is an increase for them in the punishment. Then they confessed their ignorance and said: ﴿لَوْ كُنّا نَسْمَعُ أوْ نَعْقِلُ ما كُنّا في أصْحابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾ [al-Mulk: 10], i.e. had we listened as one listens who takes in and reflects, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze; or had we reasoned as one reasons who discerns and considers, we would not be among the people of the Fire.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿فاعْتَرَفُوا بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسُحْقًا﴾ — it is also transmitted as ”فَسُحُقًا“ with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ. ”سُحْقًا“ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is "may Allah remove them far away (asḥaqahum) with a removal," i.e. may Allah distance them from His mercy. ”اَلسَّحِيقُ“ is the distant.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿فامْشُوا في مَناكِبِها﴾ means: on its mountains; and it is said: on its sides; and it is said: on its roads. The most likely interpretation — and Allah knows best — is that of those who said "on its mountains," because His saying ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأرْضَ ذَلُولا﴾ means "He made travelling on it easy for you"; and if travelling on its mountains is possible for you, that is the utmost in making it subservient.

His saying: ﴿وَإلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ﴾ means: Allah, who created the heavens without pillars and without inconsistency in them, and created the earth and made it subservient to you, is able to resurrect (yunshira) you, i.e. to raise you.

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا هي تَمُورُ﴾ — the meaning of ”تَمُورُ“ is: it revolves (heaves).

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿أنْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكم حاصِبًا﴾ means: just as He sent upon the people of Lūṭ the stones that pelted them.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى الطَّيْرِ فَوْقَهم صافّاتٍ ويَقْبِضْنَ﴾ — He made clear to them, by the creation of the heavens and the earths, what points them to His oneness; and He made (it) clear to them by subjecting the birds in the air of the sky, spreading their wings and folding them: ﴿ما يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إلا الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ — by His power.

zajjaj:22-22.t: ﴿أفَمَن يَمْشِي مُكِبًّا عَلى وجْهِهِ أهْدى أمَّنْ يَمْشِي سَوِيًّا عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the believer is following the straight path, and that the disbeliever in his error is like one who walks prone upon his face. It has come in the exegesis that the disbeliever will walk on his face in the Hereafter: «The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "How will they walk on their faces?" He said: "The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces."»

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأوْهُ زُلْفَةً سِيئَتْ وُجُوهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ — it was also read ”سُيْئَتْ“, giving the sīn a tinge (ishmām) of ḍamma; and ”سِيَتْ“ is permissible, dropping the hamza and casting its vowel onto the yāʾ. The meaning is: "When they saw the punishment near (zulfa), i.e. close, the faces of those who disbelieved were grieved: evil became apparent in them." ﴿وَقِيلَ هَذا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَدَّعُونَ﴾ — it was also read ”تَدْعُونَ“, from ”دَعَوْتُ، أدْعُو“. As for ”تَدَّعُونَ“, it has come in the exegesis: "you deny." Its interpretation in the language is: "This is that on account of which you used to make false and lying claims," i.e. you used to claim that when you died and became dust and bones you would not be brought forth. Whoever read ”تَدْعُونَ“, undoubled, the meaning is: "This is what you used to seek to hasten, calling on Allah in your saying: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ أوِ ائْتِنا بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32]." It is also possible that the meaning of ”تَدَّعُونَ“ is this as well: ”تَفْتَعِلُونَ“ from ”اَلدُّعاءُ“ (calling), and (alternatively) ”تَفْتَعِلُونَ“ from ”اَلدَّعْوى“ (claiming); that is possible — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ أصْبَحَ ماؤُكم غَوْرًا﴾ means: sunk (ghāʾir). It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with which a noun is described, so you say ”ماءٌ غَوْرٌ“, ”ماءانِ غَوْرٌ“ and ”مِياهٌ غَوْرٌ“, just as you say ”هَذا عَدْلٌ“, ”هَذانِ عَدْلٌ“ and ”هَؤُلاءِ عَدْلٌ“. The meaning of ”مَعِينٌ“ is: flowing from springs; and it has come in the exegesis: on the surface, the meaning being that it appears from the springs.
